in_scope_clauses.summary:
Validation of QMS software — software used in the QMS shall be
validated prior to initial use and after changes. For Open QMS-on-
GitHub deployments, the adopter validates GitHub configuration
plus the Open QMS engine + module manifests for intended use.

Medical device file — a compilation of documents for each medical
device type or family, including device description, intended use,
labeling, specifications, manufacturing/packaging/storage/handling/
distribution specs, measurement procedures, installation and
servicing procedures where applicable.

Document control — approval prior to issue, review/update with
re-approval, identification of changes and current revision status,
availability at points of use, legibility, prevention of unintended
use of obsolete documents.

Control of records — records shall remain legible, readily
identifiable, and retrievable. Storage, protection, retrieval,
retention period, and disposition defined.

Management review — top management shall review the QMS at planned
intervals to ensure continuing suitability, adequacy, and
effectiveness. Inputs: feedback, complaint handling, internal audit
results, CAPA status, process performance and product conformity,
regulatory and standards changes, supplier performance, risk
management updates, resource adequacy, recommendations. Outputs:
decisions and actions improving QMS effectiveness, improving
product, resource needs.

Infrastructure — including information systems. Documented
infrastructure qualification covering GitHub platform configuration,
cloud dependency, on-prem option, and backup strategy.

Design and development — planning, inputs, outputs, review,
verification, validation, transfer, changes. Traceability between
inputs, outputs, verification, and validation at every stage.

Purchasing — documented process for evaluation and selection of
suppliers based on their ability to supply product meeting the
organization's requirements; periodic re-evaluation; criteria
for selection / evaluation / monitoring / re-evaluation
proportionate to the risk of the supplied product.

Complaint handling — documented procedures for timely complaint
handling, including receipt, evaluation, investigation, reporting to
regulatory authorities where required, and record retention.

Monitoring and measurement of processes — apply suitable methods
for monitoring and (where applicable) measurement of QMS processes;
these methods shall demonstrate the ability of processes to achieve
planned results.

Internal audit — conduct audits at planned intervals to determine
whether the QMS conforms to planned arrangements and to applicable
regulatory requirements. Auditor independence required.

Management responsibility — quality policy, organization (including
management with executive responsibility and management
representative), quality planning. §820.20(c) management review is
isolated as a separate clause for sharper traceability.

Management review — management with executive responsibility shall
review the suitability and effectiveness of the quality system at
defined intervals and with sufficient frequency. Reviews must be
documented. Subset of the broader §820.20 Management
responsibility section; this entry isolates the periodic-review
requirement specifically.

Quality audit — established procedures for planned and documented
quality audits to assure the quality system is in compliance with
QMS requirements. Auditors shall not have responsibility for the
matters audited.

Design controls — plans, inputs, outputs, reviews, verification,
validation, transfer, changes.
Document controls — approval and distribution, changes.

Purchasing controls — each manufacturer shall establish and
maintain procedures to ensure that all purchased or otherwise
received product and services conform to specified requirements.
Includes evaluation of suppliers, contractors, and consultants;
type and extent of control proportionate to product / supplier
criticality; records of acceptable suppliers.

Production and process controls — including environmental controls,
personnel cleanliness, contamination control, equipment, and
production process changes. Documented production SOPs required.

Nonconforming product — procedures for control of product that
does not conform to specified requirements. Identification,
documentation, evaluation, segregation, disposition.

Corrective and preventive action (CAPA) — procedures for analyzing
processes, work operations, concessions, quality audit reports,
quality records, complaints, returned product, etc., to identify
existing and potential causes of nonconforming product. Verifying
or validating CAPA effectiveness.

General records requirements — all records required by Part 820
shall be maintained and readily available for FDA inspection.
Retention period: lifetime of device but no less than 2 years.
Records protected against loss, deterioration, unauthorized
alteration.

Complaint files — formally designated unit for complaint receipt,
review, and evaluation. Records of investigation, reportability
assessment, and disposition. PHI/PII handling architecturally
compartmentalized; see docs/guide/complaints.md.

Validation of systems — procedures and controls for closed
systems shall include validation of systems to ensure accuracy,
reliability, consistent intended performance, and the ability to
discern invalid or altered records.

Generate accurate and complete copies of records — both in human-
readable and electronic form suitable for FDA inspection, review,
and copying.

Protection of records — access limited to authorized individuals.
Implemented via GitHub Teams, branch protection, repository
permissions (with the documented caveat that GitHub permissions
are repo-level, not document-level — see PHI/PII compartmentalization
decision in docs/guide/complaints.md).

Audit trail — computer-generated, time-stamped, independent of
operators, available for FDA review. Git history + GitHub
Enterprise audit log; force-push disabled; GPG-signed commits.

Operational system checks — enforce sequencing of steps and
events. GitHub Actions workflows + required status checks +
branch-protection rules. The release-gate.yml workflow gates
release on completeness of required activities.

Signature manifestations — signed records shall display the
printed name, date/time, and meaning of the signature. Bridged
in Open QMS by the commit-trailer convention
(Signature-Meaning / Signature-Role / Signature-Justification)
plus the engine's parser and Part 11 audit-trail exporter.

Signature/record linking — signatures shall be cryptographically
bound to their respective records. Implemented via GPG-signed
commits enforced by org-level "Require signed commits."

General requirements for e-signatures — each signature unique to
one individual, identity verified before establishing.
Implemented via HR-attested GitHub identity mapping documented
in docs/guide/gpg-signing.md §2.

E-signature components — at minimum two distinct identification
components (e.g. user ID + password). GitHub SSO + MFA enforced
at org level satisfies the two-factor requirement.

Controls for identification codes / passwords — including
uniqueness, periodicity of revisions, loss management,
transaction safeguards. Implemented via GitHub / IdP password
policy referenced in docs/guide/gpg-signing.md.

QMS shall address all parts of Annex IX and cover risk management,
clinical evaluation, post-market surveillance, vigilance, supplier
controls, and product-realization processes.

Technical documentation — device description, design and
manufacturing information, GSPR compliance, benefit-risk analysis,
product verification/validation. Per-product, structured for
notified-body review.

General Safety and Performance Requirements (GSPRs) — 23 numbered
requirements across three chapters (general requirements, design
and manufacture, information supplied with the device). Each
applicable GSPR must be evaluated for conformity with documented
evidence; non-applicable GSPRs require justification. The GSPR
conformity checklist is a required component of the technical file
per Annex II §4.

Conformity assessment based on QMS and technical documentation
assessment. QMS procedures plus audit evidence of QMS operation
via Git history and issue/PR records form the auditable substrate.

Clinical evaluation — assessment of clinical safety, performance,
and benefit-risk of the device throughout its lifecycle. Clinical
evaluation plan, data identification (literature / clinical
experience / clinical investigations / equivalence), data
appraisal, analysis against acceptability criteria, conclusions,
update cadence per risk class. Output: Clinical Evaluation Report.

Post-Market Clinical Follow-up (PMCF) — proactive collection and
evaluation of clinical data from devices on the market. PMCF plan
with specific objectives and methods (registries, surveys, PMS
data, literature surveillance, PMCF studies), schedule per risk
class, PMCF evaluation report integration with CER updates and
risk-management re-evaluation.

General requirements for risk management — risk management process,
management responsibility, qualification of personnel, risk
management plan, risk management file.

Risk analysis — intended use and reasonably foreseeable misuse,
identification of characteristics related to safety, identification
of hazards and hazardous situations, estimation of risks.

Risk evaluation — for each identified hazardous situation, decide
whether risk reduction is required against the risk acceptability
criteria in the risk management plan.

Risk control — analysis of options (inherent safety / protective
measures / information for safety), implementation, verification of
implementation and effectiveness, evaluation of any new risks the
controls themselves introduce, and overall residual risk evaluation.

Evaluation of overall residual risk — explicit determination by top
management that the overall residual risk of the device, weighed
against expected benefits of the intended use, is acceptable.

Risk management review and report — review of execution of the risk
management plan and production of the risk management report.

Production and post-production activities — collection and review of
information from production and post-production phases; loop back
into the risk management process when new information affects the
risk evaluation.

Software development planning — establish and document a software
development plan covering processes, activities, deliverables,
configuration management, problem-resolution approach, and
reference to risk-management and SOUP procedures.

Software requirements analysis — define and document software
requirements from the system requirements; include functional,
performance, interface, regulatory, and risk-control requirements.
Verify and approve the requirements.

Software architectural design — transform requirements into a
documented architecture; identify software items and segregation
between items of different software safety classes; specify
interfaces; identify SOUP items and their integration constraints.

Software detailed design — refine the software items into software
units; document detailed design of each unit sufficient to
implement and test. For Class C software, document detailed design
to the depth required by the architectural decomposition.

Software unit implementation and verification — implement units,
establish and apply unit acceptance criteria, verify each unit
against the criteria, document the verification.

Software integration testing — integrate software units per the
integration plan, develop and execute integration tests, document
results, evaluate problems found.

Software release — verify all activities are complete, document
known residual anomalies and their evaluation, archive sufficient
configuration items to reproduce the release, document version
identification.

Software maintenance — establish and execute a software
maintenance plan; problem reports become maintenance inputs;
modifications follow the same lifecycle processes as new
development.

Software risk management — for each software contributing to a
hazardous situation, identify potential causes, perform risk
control, verify risk control effectiveness. Integrates with the
device-level RMF.

SOUP configuration management — document title, manufacturer,
version designation, and unique identifier for each SOUP item;
maintain the SOUP configuration record across the software life
cycle.

Software problem resolution — establish a problem resolution
process; document, investigate, and evaluate problems; implement
changes; verify changes do not introduce new problems; update
affected items (RMF, SRS, SAD, test plan).

Usability engineering process (consolidated §5.1-§5.9): prepare
use specification, user interface specification, identify primary
operating functions, hazard-related use scenarios, UI of primary
operating functions, formative evaluation, summative evaluation.
Usability Engineering File compiles the evidence.

General requirements for basic safety and essential performance —
test reports and risk-management file. Test reports typically from
external accredited labs (EMC, electrical safety). Indexed in the
technical-file index and linked from the verification protocol.

Packaged-Products Weighing 150 lb (68 kg) or Less (Partial
Simulation) — test protocols (atmospheric conditioning, vibration,
drop, compression), test sample sizes, acceptance criteria.

Packaged-Products for Parcel Delivery System Shipment — extended
test sequences for the parcel-delivery distribution environment.

Medical Device Single Audit Program — composite audit model
satisfying FDA + Health Canada + ANVISA + PMDA + TGA requirements
against a unified ISO 13485-based program. Audit evidence
assembled from the same artifact set rather than duplicated.

Policies for information security — defined, approved by management,
published, communicated to and acknowledged by relevant personnel
and interested parties, and reviewed at planned intervals or when
significant changes occur.

Legal, statutory, regulatory, and contractual requirements relevant
to information security shall be identified, documented, and kept
up to date. The organization's approach to meeting each shall be
defined.

Separation of development, test, and production environments —
including separation of duties where appropriate — to reduce the
risk of unauthorized access or unauthorized changes to the
operational environment.
